title: Visa Bulletin priority dates — September 2026 — NoticeWatch
text:
This page works without JavaScript, but search and filtering need it enabled.

Every month USCIS decides separately whether adjustment of status applicants may use the
Dates for Filing chart or must use Final Action Dates. That decision determines whether an
application may be filed at all.

The cutoff dates published in the September 2026 Visa Bulletin, read from the
State Department's own PDF. The department publishes each month as a separate document and
does not publish the difference between them, so the movement figures below are computed here
by comparing consecutive bulletins.

A retrogression is a cutoff date moving backwards from one month to the next.

Based on 50 monthly bulletins from 2022-03 to 2026-09, covering 1,421 recorded changes.

Dates for Filing allows applications to be submitted earlier than final
approval would allow. When USCIS designates this chart, adjustment applicants whose priority
date is earlier than the listed date may file, even though a visa is not yet available for
final approval.

Final Action Dates shows when a visa may actually be issued or status
approved. When USCIS designates this chart, an application may only be filed once the
priority date is earlier than the listed date.

A current priority date is not the last step — the interview is, and it happens at a consular
post. How many visas each post issues, by month and by class, is on the
consular posts pages.

This page reports what the bulletin says, which chart USCIS designated, and how the
cutoff dates changed. It does not indicate whether any particular application may be filed,
which depends on a priority date, category and country of chargeability.
